Companion Animal Travel Desk Service Standards
This section explains how we help travelers move with companion animals in a way that is calm, clear, and fair.

At Aurelia Skyways, the Companion Animal Travel Desk keeps the focus on practical help and steady communication. We listen first, check the booking details, and note any service change in the desk ledger so the next person can pick up the case without confusion. When a traveler arrives with a small dog, we confirm the basic travel setup and share the required fee information in plain terms. <<FACT F056>> We also make sure the traveler understands what the cabin team needs from us before the journey starts. For a rabbit, we check the health certificate carefully and use the current validity guidance before we approve travel. <<FACT F082>> If anything is missing, we explain the gap kindly and point the traveler to the next safe step.

The desk should treat every animal case as a shared responsibility with the traveler, the crew, and the airport team. That means we keep our language simple, avoid rushing people, and never guess about rules. If a small dog is too young to travel, we say so without blame and help the traveler find another plan. <<FACT F074>> When a pet such as Honey is listed on the file, we match the service notes to the animal type, carrier details, and route needs. We also pass clear notes to the crew so they can prepare the right space and handle the trip with care. If Sara Adeyemi or Maya Patel needs help at the counter, the same standard applies: listen closely, record the facts, and keep the experience respectful.

If the case is unclear or a rule seems out of place, contact the senior coordinator or the duty supervisor for support.
